title: Model Tells You Where to Merge: Adaptive KV Cache Merging for LLMs on Long-Context Tasks

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to compress the KV cache of LLMs for long-context inference under constrained memory budgets without significant performance degradation. This objective is shared by multiple prior papers that address KV cache compression to reduce memory consumption while maintaining performance. For example, [1] explicitly states, "Existing methods rely on dropping unimportant tokens or quantizing all entries uniformly... to accelerate generation speed for large language models (LLMs) inference." Similarly, [4] discusses adaptive KV cache merging for long-context tasks to mitigate memory consumption. Both papers aim to address the same problem-class level objective of efficient KV cache compression for constrained memory budgets.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, KVMerger, formulates KV cache merging as a constrained clustering problem solved by a specialized greedy merging-set identification algorithm, followed by a Gaussian kernel weighted merging function. This specific approach is not covered by any prior paper. While [4] introduces adaptive KV cache merging, it does not employ constrained clustering or Gaussian kernel-based merging. Papers like [14] and [18] discuss token merging methods, but these are applied to different domains (e.g., vision transformers) and do not involve constrained clustering or Gaussian kernel-based merging. Papers such as [13] and [21] discuss Gaussian kernels and clustering, but they are unrelated to KV cache compression in LLMs.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design uses benchmarks like LongBench, ZeroScrolls, and Needle-in-a-Haystack, comparing KVMerger against H2O, CaM, and full cache setups. LongBench is explicitly mentioned in [16], which introduces it as a benchmark for long-context understanding. ZeroScrolls and Needle-in-a-Haystack are part of the same benchmark family for long-context tasks. The evaluation design (benchmark family and metric semantics) is therefore covered by [16].

### Domain
The domain is efficient LLM inference, specifically KV cache compression. This application area is extensively covered by prior papers, including [1], [4], [5], [6], and [7], all of which focus on KV cache compression for LLM inference. While the specific sub-problems, datasets, or instances may differ, the general application area is the same.
